text:
customer-support: AcmeCorp (acct: ACME-PROD) opened a Sev2 — sudden spike of 429s (~80% failing) starting 09:03 UTC. They say their dedicated pool didn’t scale. CS ticket #7891, attaching customer logs: ```ERROR attach: denied: iam: serviceaccount token expired
status=403 requestId=abc123
...
init: container "warm-init" OOMKilled
imagePullBackOff for repo/redwood/attach:latest``` Please triage.

sre-bot: alert: dedicated-pool-acme-prod high-429s | probe_failures=95% | autoscaler.desired=6 autoscaler.current=2 queued_requests=14 | alert_id=DL-9832 :rotating_light:

morgan: @oncall-eng grabbing this. Any quick mitigation while we triage? :eyes:

eli: Can you paste the attach/warm-pool logs from the affected time window? Suspect either imagePull/auth or init-container OOM. Also did they rotate service account keys right before the spike?

customer-support: Pasting relevant snippets from customer: ```2026-01-12T09:02:12Z INFO rotation: service account tokens rotated by ops (reason=scheduled)
2026-01-12T09:03:01Z ERROR attach: denied: iam: serviceaccount token expired
2026-01-12T09:03:05Z WARN pod/warm-init OOMKilled
2026-01-12T09:03:09Z ERROR kubelet: ImagePullBackOff repo/redwood/attach:latest
``` They confirm SA rotation at 09:02 UTC.

tanvi: I’ve seen this exact sequence before — token rotate -> attach requests get 403 -> warm-pool attach fails -> autoscaler sees failing probes and stalls ramp (it treats repeated probe failures as unhealthy rather than transient attach-deny). If init-container OOMs happen on top, readiness never succeeds so nodes don't count toward available capacity. Repro I used: 1) force SA rotation 2) trigger 2x normal QPS surge 3) observe attach-deny for ~90-150s -> autoscaler desired grows but current stuck because readiness probes never pass.

morgan: Can we reproduce in staging? We need clear repro steps to fix autoscaler logic.

eli: Repro checklist I recommend for staging:
- rotate SA token for dedicated-pool serviceaccount
- spike load using `wrk` against dedicated route (~200 RPS) for 2m
- tail warmpool attach logs: `kubectl -n redwood logs -l app=dedicated-attach -c attach --since=10m`
- watch autoscaler decisions: `kubectl -n redwood get hpa,dedicatedpolicy -o wide`
Also check node events: `kubectl get events --sort-by=.lastTimestamp | tail -n 50`

oncall-eng: Immediate mitigation applied: manual scale run -> `redwoodctl dedicated scale --pool acme-prod --replicas 10` (ran 09:07 UTC). Warmed 7/10 pods in ~45s, traffic backfilled, 429s dropped to ~2%. Temporary config changes: probe timeout bumped to 30s and preflight image-pull gate disabled for acme-prod for the next 2h. Kept minReplicas at 3 as a safety floor.

tanvi: Good. Long-term proposals: 1) treat attach-deny/403 during attach as transient — autoscaler should mark it as retryable and prefer manual warmpool priming instead of decreasing desired; 2) add grace for SA rotation windows (accept previous tokens for ~2m); 3) bump init-container memory limits to avoid OOMs during attach churn; 4) add alert for consecutive attach-deny > 10 in 1m.

eli: Filed INF-1293 (infra) with logs, timeline, and suggested autoscaler patches. Linked playbook for triage: https://redwood.internal/triage/INF-1293 (contains repro steps above + sample logs).

customer-support: AcmeCorp confirmed post-mitigation: requests failing dropped from 80% -> 2%. They appreciated the manual scaling. Asked for RCA and timeline to share with their ops team.

morgan: Action items assigned: 
1) Reproduce in staging using eli + tanvi (owner: eli, tanvi) — target: reproduce by EOD today.
2) Patch autoscaler to treat attach-deny as transient (owner: infra team, issue INF-1293) — target: next sprint.
3) Add dashboard tile for attach-deny rate + alert (owner: eng-sre) — target: 72h.
4) Increase init-container mem limit for attach image and add CI regression for OOM (owner: eng-runtime) — target: next sprint.
5) Customer comms (owner: morgan) — send timeline + mitigation steps.

oncall-eng: Closing alert for now — will keep thread open for follow-up. Please drop postmortem link when ready and ping #postmortems. :white_check_mark:
